newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan mulls listings by overseas holding firms.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan mulls listings by overseas holding firms.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Wednesday it was considering allowing foreign and local holding companies to list stock in the domestic market to help internationalise the island's economy.
"Our commission has authorised the Taiwan Stock Exchange Corporation to complete a proposal that would allow listings by both foreign and local holding companies," a commission official told Reuters.
"It's part of our drive to develop Taiwan into an Asia-Pacific operations centre," he said by telephone.
Details have yet to be set, the official said.
"So far, the exchange hasn't set all the details and has yet to submit the proposal to us," he said.
Several foreign holding companies have already expressed an interest to list in the domestic stock market.
"Several foreign firms have enquired us about the possibility of listing in our stock market," he said.
Taiwan now forbids listings by holding companies, but hopes to ease the policy, he said.
"It should be done in our further liberalisation to attract multinational companies."
Taiwan has embarked on an ambitious reform drive to woo the Asia-Pacific operations centres of major transnational firms, including liberalisation of its financial markets and investment policies.
